resale_co.name: Certificate of Resale or Change of Tenancy (Property Resale or Change of Tenancy Certificate)
resale_co.issued_by: Hazlet Township Code Inspection Bureau (Code Official / Code Enforcement Office)
resale_co.valid_for: Six months from the date of issuance; a renewal or extension costs $35
requirements: Step 1: Construction Permit Clearance Release from the Code Enforcement Department confirming there are no open permits; no certificate is issued while any permit is open
Step 2: Fire Compliance Certificate from the Hazlet Township Bureau of Fire Prevention (Hazlet Fire District #1)
Step 3: Certificate of Resale from the Township Code Official after a general visual inspection for unsafe conditions under the Property Maintenance Code (2012 IPMC as adopted)
A temporary certificate may be issued at the Code Official's discretion if there are no apparent life-safety issues

A home in disrepair may be transferred "as is" if the buyer requests a title transfer certificate in writing with an affidavit assuming all risk; no occupancy until the Code Official finds no life-safety issues

fees.label: Certificate of resale inspection, multifamily, per unit
Residential reinspection (one reinspection is included; each later one)
Certificate renewal or extension
fees.quote: The certificate of resale or change of tenancy renewal or extension fee shall be $35.

fees.label: Construction permit clearance release, multifamily, per unit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Register for the Property Resale or Change of Tenancy Certificate on the Township's SDL Portal (www.sdlportal.com, Hazlet Township), where fees can be paid by credit card or e-check and inspections requested. Get the items in this order: Construction Permit Clearance Release, then the Fire Compliance Certificate from the Bureau of Fire Prevention, then the Certificate of Resale from the Code Official. Fees are paid when the application is filed.

evidence.quote: Be advised as of September 1, 2025 Hazlet Township has made new requirements for any resale, change of ownership, change of occupancy, or change of tenancy.
Get started today! Register for a Property Resale or Change of Tenancy Certificate

A certificate of resale or change of tenancy must be obtained in connection with any sale, resale, rental, lease, change of occupancy, or transfer of title or ownership of any property containing a structure(s) intended to be used for human habitation or commercial use.
No certificate of resale or change of tenancy shall be issued if there are any open permits.
Any certificate of resale or change of tenancy issued pursuant to this article shall be valid for six months from the date of issuance.

resale_co.notes: Township code Chapter 170 (Code Inspection Bureau, amended by Ord. Nos. 1771-25 and 1778-25 in 2025) was read through the ecode360 text reader. The program started September 1, 2025. The Code Inspection Bureau office is at 1766 Union Avenue per the code. The Code Enforcement Officer's email is behind a web contact form, so none is listed. Each inspection fee includes one reinspection. Rental-only items (residential rental license, landlord registration, lead-safe certificates for rentals at $75 / $125) are not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level including the basement near the stairs, within 10 feet of bedrooms, and inside all bedrooms (Hazlet requirement); 10-year sealed battery or interconnected hardwired; hardwired alarms may not be replaced with battery units; all smoke alarms under 10 years old
Carbon monoxide alarms on each level with sleeping areas, within 10 feet of bedrooms; one in the attic if it has a fuel-burning appliance; CO alarms must be under 5 years old
Secondary power source label ("CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER") within 18 inches of the main electrical panel if there is a generator, solar panels, battery storage or other supplemental source

Inspector also checks house numbers (at least 4 inches), exterior cleanliness, utilities on, electrical panel and GFCI outlets, thumb-latch deadbolts, 20-minute garage entry door, window locks, handrails on 4 or more risers, metal dryer hose
A Construction Permit Clearance letter (no open permits) must be on file before the fire certificate is approved

authorities.lead_time: Pay online, then request an inspection date within 7 to 10 days of the closing; approval is pending the Bureau's review. Certificates are non-transferable.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online only with the Residential Resale - Change of Ownership - Change of Tenant Application (linked from the Fire District site) and pay the fee during the application. Get the Construction Permit Clearance from the Township first. Questions go to the Bureau of Fire Prevention, 812 Poole Ave, Hazlet, 732-264-1427.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (thorner@hazletfiredistrict.org); Michelle Barney, Administrative Clerk, handles applications

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Fire Compliance is required as per N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 for residential dwellings at time of resale, change of tenancy, or change of occupancy.
The inspection date request should be within 7-10 days of the closing
Hazlet Twp. Fire Bureau also requires Smoke Detectors in all bedrooms.
Fire Official, The Bureau of Fire Prevention
LEAID: 1339-001 Hazlet Twp ... Enf Auth. District ... Fire Official Thomas Horner Phone (732) 264-1700 ... Email thorner@hazletfiredistrict.org

fire_cert.notes: The Fire District charges a flat $75.00 with a $25.00 re-inspection fee; no rush tiers are published. The state fire directory lists phone (732) 264-1700 and 1766 Union Ave, but the Fire District's own contact page gives 812 Poole Ave and 732-264-1427. The Township code (Section 170-8C) also says the certificate of resale is revoked if the smoke/CO certificate is not obtained before occupancy. The checklist does not list a fire extinguisher, consistent with P.L.2025, c.19. Note the checklist's stricter local rules: smoke alarms in every bedroom and CO alarms under 5 years old.

other_items.label: Construction Permit Clearance Release (no open permits)
other_items.detail: Required first, before the fire certificate and the certificate of resale. Fee $65 for a single-family home. Any open permits must be documented, inspected and closed through the Construction Department. The fire checklist calls this a Letter of No Interest.
